ratio_rationale: The archetypal poster-driven meeting: the programme IS the abstract book, and the sheet already records a dated 2001-2006 study putting it at ~13,000+ abstracts a year against ~30,000 attendees — 43%, which is context for this judgement, not a finding of ours. Sits with ECR 48% and ATS 50% among counted rows. Judged slightly below that dated implied rate at 40%. Clears the bar by an order of magnitude on any plausible ratio.
programme_evidence: poster-dominated neuroscience meeting; 2,500 late-breaking cap alone implies scale

ratio_rationale: Session-led regulatory-affairs meeting — the programme is built from invited panels and tracks, with a modest professional/student poster programme attached. That is the EuroPCR (6%) shape rather than a research congress. The existing sheet note already reads "likely FAILS the bar". 8% of 5,000 is ~400, nowhere near 1,000.
programme_evidence: session-led regulatory meeting with a modest poster programme

ratio_rationale: National cardiology research congress whose abstracts publish as Clinical Research in Cardiology supplements — a real contributed backbone. Anchored on ESC at 15%, the only counted cardiology row, and nudged up because a national congress draws a higher presenting share than a global one where many attend to learn. 20% of 8,700 is ~1,740.
programme_evidence: abstracts publish as Clinical Research in Cardiology supplements; 8,700 attendees (2026)

ratio_rationale: Multidisciplinary surgical congress with a genuine ANZ J Surg supplement, so a high presenting share is right — judged at 40%, near DDW 37% and SOT 46%. But the delegate base is small (more than 1,750), so even a generous ratio gives ~700. It would need ~57% to reach the bar. NOTE the supplement is countable at rung 3 (ANZ J Surg 95(S1), 211 pages) — a real count should replace this estimate.
programme_evidence: ANZ J Surg 95(S1) abstract supplement; 500+ lectures incl. invited speakers

ratio_rationale: Focused specialty congress with a Cephalalgia abstract supplement each edition — the shape where most delegates present, so judged at 35% near UEG/ASN. The constraint is size: 1,600 delegates gives ~560. It would need 63% to clear. NOTE the supplement is countable at rung 3 (Cephalalgia, doi 10.1177/03331024251366059) — a real count should replace this estimate.
programme_evidence: Cephalalgia abstract supplement per edition; over 1,600 delegates from 90+ countries

ratio_rationale: Large professional convention: 2,500+ sessions, but the sheet notes many are CE rather than research, so this is NOT a 40%+ congress. It does run a competitive Call for Papers feeding a large poster and technical-session programme, which puts it above the pure teaching meetings. Judged 15%, level with ESC and above AAD 9%. 15% of ~15,000 is ~2,250. Robust to the judgement: even at 8% it clears the bar, which is why this is an INCLUDE despite the uncertainty about the CE share.
programme_evidence: 2,500+ sessions, many CE-eligible, alongside a competitive Call for Papers

ratio_rationale: A CE and trade meeting: 30,000+ people come for courses and the exhibit floor, and the only contributed science is a student-led poster session. Same shape as Yankee Dental Congress, already on the removed list for exactly this reason. Judged 2% — below EuroPCR 6% — and even that gives ~600. This row is the clearest demonstration that attendance alone would mislead: the biggest headcount in this batch produces almost no submitted science.
programme_evidence: CE course catalogue plus exhibit floor; student-led scientific poster session only
